From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up: discovery recap and next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking time yesterday to walk through Finlay's inference needs. Quick recap from my side and two proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Recap (high level)
- Current priority: pilot to validate latency/cost for document-processing pipelines (PDF/paragraph extraction)
- Constraint: must run in our EU cloud region or on-prem for a subset of sensitive datasets
- Success metric: p99 latency < 450ms on 1kqps-style bursts, cost < $0.03/1k tokens for steady-state

Open questions for you
1) Which dataset types will you want to keep in your VPC vs hosted? (rough percentages help)
2) Who owns procurement and security sign-off?
3) Is there an internal timeline for a pilot decision (target month)?

Proposed next steps
- Option A: 30-minute technical pairing + quick pilot template (we scope data, infra, and a narrow eval set)
- Option B: 20-minute pricing/contract primer with Ben to discuss reserved capacity and SSO/KMS integration

I've attached a short one-pager and an architecture sketch that maps to what we discussed (attachment stubs below). If helpful, here are three calendar windows: Wed 4/18 10:00–10:30 PT, Thu 4/19 14:00–14:30 PT, Mon 4/23 09:30–10:00 PT.

Attachment: Discovery_Recap_Redwood_v1.pdf (1-page recap)
Attachment: architecture-diagram.png (inference flow + network zones)

If you prefer, I can loop Ben in to discuss pilot sizing/pricing right away. Appreciate any quick direction on priority so we can tailor the pilot scope.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the write-up and the clear options. Two quick notes: 

- We're still in the evaluation phase; main blockers are cost modeling and internal security checklist (will need KMS + audit logs).
- For now, EU-hosted would be preferred vs full on-prem; a hybrid plan could work depending on the pilot cost.

Timeline: hoping to decide whether to pilot by end of May, but not firm. Procurement person is copied on the internal thread (I'll introduce them if we get to pricing).

I'll review the one-pager this afternoon and get back with availability for a call next week.

— Alex
